title: Package managers side by side
summary: The same jobs in apt, dnf, zypper, pacman and apk, and installing a vendor .deb offline.

steps.title: Two layers
body: Every family has a **low-level** tool that installs a single package file, and a **high-level** tool that talks to repositories and resolves dependencies:
| Family | Low level (one file) | High level (repos + dependencies) |
| RHEL / Fedora | `rpm` (`.rpm`) | `dnf` (older: `yum`; RHEL 8+ `yum` is an alias for dnf) |
You almost always use the high-level tool. `dpkg -i` / `rpm -i` on a downloaded file do **not** fetch its dependencies; `apt install ./file.deb` and `dnf install ./file.rpm` do.

steps.prompt: Match the low-level tool to its high-level partner.

steps.title: The equivalence table
body: | Job | apt | dnf | zypper | pacman | apk |
| refresh the index | `apt update` | `dnf check-update` (or `makecache`) | `zypper refresh` | `pacman -Sy` | `apk update` |
| upgrade everything | `apt upgrade` | `dnf upgrade` | `zypper update` | `pacman -Syu` | `apk upgrade` |
| install | `apt install x` | `dnf install x` | `zypper install x` | `pacman -S x` | `apk add x` |
| remove | `apt remove x` | `dnf remove x` | `zypper remove x` | `pacman -R x` | `apk del x` |
| search | `apt search x` | `dnf search x` | `zypper search x` | `pacman -Ss x` | `apk search x` |
| details | `apt show x` | `dnf info x` | `zypper info x` | `pacman -Si x` | `apk info x` |

On Arch never run `pacman -Sy x` alone (a partial upgrade can break libraries): install with `pacman -S x` after a full `pacman -Syu`. In Dockerfiles: `apt-get update && apt-get install -y x`, `dnf install -y x`, `apk add --no-cache x`.

steps.title: Install a vendor .deb without the internet
prompt: A vendor sent two packages, now in `~/pkgs`. This machine has no network, so only what is already installed can
1. Look inside them first: `dpkg-deb -I FILE` shows the control data (version, `Depends`), `dpkg-deb -c FILE` the files.
2. Install `hello-shop` with **apt**, so its dependencies are checked: `sudo apt install ./FILE.deb` (the `./` tells apt
it is a file, not a package name). Then run `hello-shop`.
3. `shop-report` cannot be installed here. Write the name of the package it depends on that this machine does not
4. Write the list of files `hello-shop` installed, as `dpkg -L` prints it, into `~/answers/files.txt`.

checks.name: hello-shop is installed
checks.fail: `hello-shop` is not installed (`dpkg -l hello-shop` should say `ii`). `sudo apt install ./pkgs/hello-shop_1.0-1_all.deb`.

checks.name: shop-report is not half-installed
checks.fail: `shop-report` is in a broken state (`dpkg -l shop-report`). `sudo dpkg -r shop-report` cleans it up; `apt` would have refused it in the first place.

checks.name: missing.txt names the missing dependency
checks.fail: `dpkg-deb -f ~/pkgs/shop-report_2.1-1_all.deb Depends` lists two packages. Which one does `dpkg -l` not know?

checks.name: files.txt is the dpkg -L list
checks.fail: `~/answers/files.txt` should hold exactly what `dpkg -L hello-shop` prints.

hints: `dpkg-deb -I ~/pkgs/hello-shop_1.0-1_all.deb` shows `Depends: jq (>= 1.6)`. `dpkg -l jq` shows it is installed.
`sudo apt install ./pkgs/hello-shop_1.0-1_all.deb` from your home folder. Without `./` apt looks for a package called `pkgs/...` in its index.
`dpkg-deb -f ~/pkgs/shop-report_2.1-1_all.deb Depends` prints `shop-lib (>= 2.0), jq`; `dpkg -l shop-lib` knows nothing about it.
explain: `dpkg -i` installs exactly one file and leaves the package broken if a dependency is missing; `apt install ./file.deb`
resolves dependencies from the configured repositories and refuses cleanly when it cannot. The same split exists
everywhere: `rpm -i` vs `dnf install ./file.rpm`, `apk add --allow-untrusted file.apk` on Alpine. In images, prefer the
vendor's repository over a downloaded file, so updates keep coming.

steps.title: Mission: packages and services
prompt: No internet, two `.deb` files and a dependency puzzle. In **Packages and services**, do **Install, offline** with `dpkg` and the dependency order it needs.
steps.explain: `dpkg -i` installs one file and complains about missing dependencies; installing them first (or `apt install ./file.deb`) solves the puzzle.
